title: The Day Erica Forgot to Wear Green
subtitle: A short St. Patrick's Day story — and the American custom behind it.
description: An A2 reading and listening story set on St. Patrick's Day, explaining the American wear-green custom, with past-tense practice, vocabulary and comprehension exercises.
passage: In the United States, March 17th is St. Patrick's Day. It began as an Irish holiday, and many Americans now celebrate it too — with parades, green decorations and, in a few cities, a river dyed bright green for the day. There is also a custom in American schools: if you forget to wear something green, your friends are allowed to pinch you.
"Oh no!" Erica said when she walked into school. Everyone was wearing green. Everyone except her. She had forgotten what day it was.
"No green? You get a pinch," said her best friend Sarah, and she walked over and pinched her arm.
"Ouch!" Erica cried. She knew it was going to be a long day if she did not find something green fast.
She went outside to look for a shamrock — a small green plant with three leaves — but she could not find one anywhere. She sat down on the steps and started to cry.
Suddenly a leprechaun appeared in front of her. In Irish stories, a leprechaun is a tiny man who guards a pot of gold.
"I'm a leprechaun, and I'm here to cheer you up on St. Paddy's Day," he replied.
"I forgot to wear green," Erica said. "If I go back inside, everyone will pinch me all day long."
"No worries," the leprechaun said. "I'll find you some green."
A pot of gold appeared beside him. He took a handful of gold and threw it into the air. Then he took off his hat and pulled out of it the most perfect shamrock Erica had ever seen.
Erica thanked him, pinned the shamrock to her shirt, and walked back into school to enjoy the rest of her day — pinch-free.

exercises.title: Understanding the Story
exercises.instructions: The questions use different words from the text. Think about the meaning, not the exact wording.

items.prompt: Why was Erica the only student not wearing green?
options: She had not remembered the date
She had arrived late for school
items.explanation: She “had forgotten what day it was”, so she had dressed without thinking about the holiday.

items.prompt: Sarah is Erica's best friend, but she pinched her. Why?
options: It is what the custom allows when someone forgets to wear green
items.explanation: The first paragraph explains the custom — it is a game, not an argument.

items.prompt: Why did Erica start crying on the steps?
options: She had searched for something green and found nothing
Sarah had gone inside without her
items.explanation: She could not find a shamrock “anywhere”, which left her with no way out of being pinched all day.

items.prompt: What does the text tell you a leprechaun is?
options: A tiny man from Irish stories who guards gold
items.explanation: The text defines it: “a tiny man who guards a pot of gold”.

items.prompt: Where did the shamrock actually come from?
items.explanation: He threw the gold in the air, but the shamrock came out from under his hat.

items.prompt: What does “pinch-free” tell you about the rest of her day?
items.explanation: The ending -free means “without”, so the problem was solved.

items.prompt: Where is this custom of pinching described as happening?
items.explanation: “There is also a custom in American schools” — the holiday is Irish in origin, but this particular custom is American.

exercises.title: Story Vocabulary
exercises.instructions: Choose the word that fits each sentence.

items.prompt: A ___ is a small green plant with three leaves.
items.explanation: A shamrock is the three-leaved plant that symbolizes Ireland.

items.prompt: Wearing green on March 17th is an American ___.
items.explanation: A custom is something people in a place usually do.

items.prompt: Her friend walked over and ___ her arm.
items.explanation: To pinch is to squeeze the skin between finger and thumb.

items.prompt: The leprechaun wanted to ___ her up.
items.explanation: To cheer someone up is to make a sad person feel happier.
"What's the matter?" is a friendly way to ask why someone is upset.

exercises.title: Telling the Story in the Past
exercises.instructions: Put each verb into the simple past.

items.prompt: Erica ___ into school and saw that everyone was in green.
She ___ down on the steps and started to cry.
A leprechaun ___ in front of her.
Erica ___ him and went back inside.

discussion: Does your country have a holiday where people wear a particular color, or a small custom like the pinching one? Describe it.
Erica's friend pinched her even though they are best friends. Is that kind of joke normal among friends where you live?
Tell the story again in your own words, in five or six sentences, using the simple past.
Write about 70 words about a day when you forgot something important. What happened?
